data.title: QuantumScape extends losses to seventh straight session
data.description:
QuantumScape widened its losing streak to the seventh straight session on Wednesday after registering steep declines in recent trading. The shares ended 2.74% lower at $3.19.

Between November 10 and November 17, shares of the lithium metal battery maker plunged more than 26% compared to a 2.4% fall in the broader markets.

On a year-to-date basis, QuantumScape has tumbled nearly 69% compared to a 7% rise in the S&P500 index.

In October, the company reported a narrower third-quarter loss of $0.14 per share. QuantumScape ended the quarter with $819.8M in liquidity and reaffirmed its full-year adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $250M to $275M and capital expenditure outlook of $27M to $37M.

As per Seeking Alpha’s quant rating, QS has a Hold rating with a score of 2.50 out of 5. The firm has been rated an F for profitability and momentum, while it has been graded a C for valuation.

Seeking Alpha analysts have assigned a Hold rating for QS with one Hold and one Sell call. Meanwhile, Wall Street analysts have seven Hold calls and 2 Strong Sell ratings for the stock. Overall, Wall Street analysts have issued a Hold call for the company.

data.title: CBOT wheat slides 4% on firming dollar, technical selling
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures fell roughly 4% on Wednesday, giving up gains from the previous session as the dollar hit a 19-month high, making US grains less competitive globally, analysts said.

  • The dollar firmed on expectations for an interest rate hike next month.

  • CBOT December soft red winter wheat settled down 25-1/4 cents, or 4.24%, at $5.70 per bushel after dipping to $5.69, the contract's lowest since January.

  • CBOT March wheat ended down 24-1/4 cents, or 3.97%, at $5.86 a bushel. Technical selling accelerated as CBOT March wheat fell below last week's low of $5.97.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended down 23-3/4 cents, or 3.75%, at $6.09-1/4 a bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) fell 10-1/2 cents, or 1.64%, to end at $6.29-1/4 a bushel.

  • Managed commodity funds appeared to be extending their net short position in CBOT wheat futures, brokers said.

  • Traders awaited a meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia for diplomatic developments on Russia's war in Ukraine.

    US President Donald Trump is expected to hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China on Thursday, in addition to the trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, US and Russian officials said.

  • Ahead of Thursday's weekly export sales report from the US Department of Agriculture, analysts expected the government to report net export sales of US wheat in the week to November 12 at 200,000 to 400,000 metric tons.

data.title: Nigeria's Arik Air to add capacity in 2027 after spike in jet fuel eases
data.description:
Nigeria's Arik Air expects to add flight capacity in 2027 as jet fuel prices stabilize, an executive said on Wednesday, after the country's airlines threatened to suspend earlier this year over high fuel costs due to the war in Iran.

Ailemen Charles Arumemi-Johnson, chief commercial officer of Arik Air, said jet fuel prices remain high. But an earlier spike due to the war in Iran has since eased and the Nigerian government is taking steps to reduce inflation, which would improve purchasing power and encourage more airline travel.

  • "We're going to add capacity because we have the market," he said in an interview on the sidelines of the International Civil Aviation Organization's global transport conference in Montreal.

  • "Once oil prices go down ticket fares become cheaper. We just hope the war in Iran ends as quickly as possible."

  • He said the carrier is looking to bring three planes back into service.

  • High jet fuel prices have led airlines globally to reduce capacity and raise fares to offset rising costs.

  • Nigerian airlines had initially threatened to ​suspend all flight operations from April 20 unless crippling jet fuel ‌prices were reduced.

  • Nigeria's Dangote Refinery, which is owned by Africa's richest man and is the biggest on the continent, has ramped up its jet fuel production to meet demand following the Middle East crisis.
